newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Bunds set to slide lower towards 99.70.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bunds set to slide lower towards 99.70.

text.p: June Bund futures traded on LIFFE gapped lower at the open and are set to decline on Friday, technical analysts said.
"I would err to the side of caution and would prefer to sell upticks rather than to sell weakness," said Simon Mattholie, senior proprietary trader at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.
"A decline back to 99.70 is certainly not out of question. But we are not likely to see that this morning, we will have to wait for a catalyst from the U.S. to get us moving this afternoon," he said.
At 0655 GMT, June Bund futures were at 100.37, down 0.19.
On daily charts 99.70 was the low on April 17.
The slide would initially be stemmed by support around 100.35, Mattholie said. In early trade Bunds dipped to 100.33.
The contract gapped down from Thursday's low at 100.55 to open at 100.43. It closed at 100.57 on Thursday and this, coupled with the gap, suggested caution, he said.
To the upside, Mattholie said initial resistance was offered at the top of the gap at 100.55.
"Really you want to get to the 100.74-75 region to initiate shorts, because it looks as if the market has turned foul and it is going to be heading lower," he said.
Richard Adcock, manager of technical research at HSBC Markets in London, said it was not really surprising that Bunds had gapped lower.
"With the momentum and the indicator background we were looking for a break of that uptrend which held into the close last night and that has obviously happened," he said.
Bunds should now rally and fill the gap, he said, although they may not manage to push much higher.
"The contract will struggle within the 100.55 to 100.65 range," said Adcock.
"The underside of the uptrend is now at 100.67, so it is certainly in that area that we are looking to sell the market again," Adcock added.
At the short end, June Euromarks were at 96.75, unchanged from Thursday's close.
